crossRefs.note: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he…
When he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.
When they sought to seize him, they feared the multitudes, because they considered him to be a prophet.

translations.web: The sergeants reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans,
translations.bsb: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
translations.kjv: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
